source.title: ptt5-v2: A Closer Look at Continued Pretraining of T5 Models for the Portuguese Language
source.authors: Marcos Piau; Roberto A. Lotufo; Rodrigo Nogueira

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across model sizes and continued-pretraining settings in Portuguese, a new language and training setting for these scaling-related questions.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream-task metrics across model sizes and pretraining amounts, which bear on V6. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fit scaling laws, and the reported training-loss overshoot is not a held-out loss scaling result. Retrieval results are included where reported as downstream performance; cited results from other papers are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Reports downstream scores for fine-tuned T5, mT5 and continued-pretrained ptt5-v2 models from 60M to 3.7B parameters, and NPM against Portuguese pretraining tokens (Figs 2, 4). These bear on V6's 'improves with scale' in a new setting: Portuguese continued pretraining of encoder-decoder models. No predictive law is fitted and no loss-to-downstream relation is reported, so this is a weak, descriptive test. Scaling is secondary to the paper's goal of releasing models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that monolingual pretraining gains diminish as model size increases. They further conclude that, at the same compute budget, a small high-quality dataset and a larger lower-quality dataset give similar downstream performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses continued T5 pretraining on Portuguese mC4-pt, then evaluates finetuned downstream tasks and rerankers; it does not fit held-out cross-entropy scaling laws or test compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream NPM varies with data quality, pretraining duration, and learning-rate schedule; inverse square root scheduling performs better through 2 epochs, while constant learning rate is better afterward, and both converge to the same final plotted value. The paper reports that the quality-filtering difference is at most approximately 2 NPM points.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the downstream metrics. The paper evaluates downstream performance rather than held-out pretraining loss, and the pretraining-token and epoch plots provide figure-only values.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported Table 3 results for the listed downstream tasks and retrieval metrics were omitted. Other retrieval-method comparisons and cited competitor results were not recorded as rows because they are not results for the study's ptt5-v2 scaling series.

untested.parts: No predictive or fitted relationship (power law or otherwise) between scale and downstream score. No relation to held-out pretraining loss. Only four sizes per family, and token scaling only for t5-base.
No held-out pretraining loss scaling reported.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Continued pretraining and repeated data are present, but no power-law form is fitted for them.
No exponent fitting. The scheduler effect on downstream NPM is not a scaling-law fit-dependence test.

missing.what: Per-model aggregate NPM column (e.g. T5 61.71/65.63/69.95/74.56; mT5 54.35/63.46/64.76/77.45; ptt5-v2 69.86/72.82/77.68/78.48), showing diminishing gains for ptt5-v2 at 3B
NPM vs non-embedding parameters including ptt5-v1 variants; ptt5-v1 base slightly beats ptt5-v2 base

record.verdict_notes: Scaling is incidental: the paper releases Portuguese T5 checkpoints. Size series compare Google's checkpoints plus fixed-token (116B) continued pretraining, so the size axis is not a controlled scaling study. The training-loss overshoot under the inverse square root schedule is not a scaling result. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Does not fit laws on small runs or compare their predictions with much larger runs.
Does not compare parameter-token allocations at fixed compute or estimate compute-optimal scaling.
Does not vary depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Uses Portuguese continued pretraining, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in this or other modalities or training regimes.

Evaluates several Portuguese downstream tasks across model sizes and some pretraining-token settings; does not test downstream predictability from held-out pretraining loss or fit a predictive relationship.
Does not estimate scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits under alternative fitting choices. The learning-rate-schedule loss overshoot is not a test of scaling-law fit dependence.

relationships.condition: T5 and ptt5-v2 size series on RTE, STS (up to ptt5-v2-large) and TweetSentBR; mT5 RTE; MonoPTT5 rerankers on all four retrieval sets; t5-base NPM vs Portuguese pretraining tokens
relationships.reason: Scores rise monotonically with size (r01-r12, r13-r16, r25-r31, r33-r36, r37-r52) and NPM rises with tokens or epochs across datasets and schedulers (r53-r57).
relationships.display_finding: Scores rise monotonically with model size across the specified language and retrieval tasks, while NPM increases with Portuguese pretraining tokens or epochs across datasets and schedulers.

relationships.condition: mT5 on TweetSentBR and STS; ptt5-v2-large vs 3B on STS
relationships.reason: Non-monotonic or negligible gains with size: mt5-large TweetSentBR drops about 9.7 F1 below mt5-base (r22, r23), mt5-large STS barely moves (r18, r19), and ptt5-v2-3B STS falls below large (r31, r32).
relationships.display_finding: mT5-large fell about 9.7 F1 below mT5-base on TweetSentBR and barely improved STS, while ptt5-v2-3B scored below ptt5-v2-large on STS.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
